name: security-agent-filesystem-root-review
intent: Agent broker file-root capabilities and grant-generation revocation
artifacts: File-tool schema, allowed roots, symlink/parent handling, broker identity and approval scope.
trace: Follow model-supplied paths through normalization and descriptor/open logic. Compare the final object to the user-authorized workspace rather than only a textual prefix.
experiment: Grant a disposable file-root capability for markerA, then narrow/revoke it and reuse the old broker handle under the declared generation policy. Compare a fresh permitted handle and the stale context without accessing real private files.
disproof: A prompt asking for an outside path is not access; an external file read by setup code must not be attributed to the agent tool.
repair: Enforce final file-object authority and retest legitimate nested paths, link/rename races in local fixtures and explicit user grants.
branch_decisions: Resolve paths at the actual file operation, including parent symlinks, directory handles and races between check and use. A lexical startswith check can misclassify sibling names, while sandboxed mount isolation may deny the path independently. Use disposable local roots and marker files; privileged fixture creation of a symlink is not proof the untrusted actor can create it.
operational_method: Specialize in broker-issued workspace/root capabilities: grant ID, canonical root, allowed operations, user/task ownership and revocation generation. Resolve the actual file descriptor/path at use and compare it with the current capability; an old tool handle must not silently retain authority after a narrowed grant if policy revokes it. Test disposable marker roots and a stale broker handle. Ordinary traversal/link mechanics without a changing agent grant belong in filesystem review.
